content: ← Our Community Explore faith Alpha Course A welcoming space to explore the basics of Christian faith, ask questions and share your point of view. What is Alpha? The parish describes Alpha as a series of sessions exploring the basics of Christian faith. It is for anyone who would like to explore, ask questions and share their point of view, whatever their background or context. What happens at a session? The format described by the parish begins with tea and cake, followed by a short film presentation on a question about Christian faith and time for discussion. The course material explores topics including Jesus, prayer, faith, the Holy Spirit, the Bible and how God guides us. Who is Alpha for? Alpha is intended for people who want space to explore Christian faith and ask questions. You do not need to have everything worked out before you come. title: Baptisms
documentTitle: Baptisms | St Michael & All Angels
description: A joyful welcome into the life of the Church. Enquiries are welcome for children and adults.
content: ← Worship LIFE EVENTS Baptisms A joyful welcome into the life of the Church. Enquiries are welcome for children and adults. Ask about baptism Children & Families What is baptism? Baptism is a significant step in the Christian faith and marks a person’s welcome into the life of the Church. The parish welcomes enquiries for children and adults. Who may be baptised? Under the parish policy agreed by the PCC in September 2026, baptism will normally be available to people who live in the parish, belong to the church, regularly worship here, are on the Electoral Roll, or have another recognised connection with the parish or church. The clergy may consider other requests where there is a strong pastoral reason and, where appropriate, may seek the consent of the candidate’s own parish priest or incumbent. Preparing for baptism Candidates—and, for a child, their parents or carers—will be offered appropriate preparation. This helps those involved understand the meaning of baptism, the promises made in the service and baptism’s place in Christian faith and the worshipping life of the church. Parents or carers should be able to make the promises with integrity. Godparents are welcome to take part in preparation where possible. Children and godparents Parents or carers take part in a child’s preparation and baptism service. Before a baptism is arranged, the parish expects the family to attend several church services to become familiar with and connected to the worshipping life of the church. Godparents are chosen by the parents or carers and must be baptised. The usual expectation is three godparents, ideally two of the same sex as the child; the minimum is two, and the policy suggests a maximum of six, with flexibility where appropriate. Someone who is not baptised may be included as a sponsor or may consider baptism before the service. Adults and older candidates Adults and older candidates receive preparation suited to their circumstances. Where appropriate, baptism may be linked with preparation for confirmation. Two or more sponsors may be chosen. When and where? Baptisms normally take place during the main Sunday morning service, usually the All-Age Worship service listed on the first Sunday of the month. Another time may be arranged for a good pastoral or practical reason, with the clergy’s agreement. In that case, the person baptised is expected to be welcomed at a main Sunday service on another occasion. Please check the Calendar for current service dates. Thanksgiving or blessing Where baptism is not possible, not desired or not yet the right step, the church may offer a service of thanksgiving or blessing. This provides an opportunity to give thanks, pray for the child or candidate and mark the occasion without the baptismal promises. How to begin Initial enquiries and bookings are made through the parish clergy or parish baptism officer. The clergy agree arrangements, ensure preparation takes place and decide how exceptional circumstances should be handled. After baptism, the church continues to welcome and support the person and their family through worship, teaching, pastoral care and appropriate information about church activities. title: Eco Church
documentTitle: Eco Church | St Michael & All Angels
description: Care for creation is part of the parish’s life and care for its churchyard. The Eco Group has encouraged practical steps for wildlife, the grounds and church life.
content: ← Visit & Learn About our parish Eco Church Care for creation is part of the parish’s life and care for its churchyard. The Eco Group has encouraged practical steps for wildlife, the grounds and church life. St Michael and All Angels Church viewed across its churchyard. The church and churchyard, pictured in the 2024 Churchyard Trail. “Reducing the causes of climate change is essential to the life of faith. It is a way to love our neighbour and to steward the gift of creation.” The Eco Group was established in 2022 to advise the PCC on local environmental action. The parish registered with the A Rocha Eco Church Award Scheme and received the Eco Church Silver Award. The supplied Churchyard Trail and award badge record this as a 2024 achievement; this page records the award received and does not claim that accreditation is currently active. Practical care for creation Our Eco Journey The parish’s source material records the following work by the Eco Group and volunteers. Hedgerow planting More than 80 metres of hedgerow were planted. The 2024 trail describes newly planted hedges around the newer churchyard as future green corridors for mammals and birds. Churchyard composting The compost area was reorganised so green waste could be composted and the resulting soil returned to areas within the churchyards. A small fruit orchard The Churchyard Trail records that an orchard was planted in winter 2022/23, with apple, pear, damson, quince and medlar trees. Garden of Remembrance Lavender and rosemary were planted around the Garden of Remembrance to provide summer nectar for insects. Wildlife-friendly mowing The trail describes the area behind the church being mown twice a year, and a three-year mowing and raking rotation in the newer churchyard, leaving areas unmown each year. Seasonal pond A rainwater-fed seasonal pond was created in 2024. The trail describes dragonflies, damselflies, pond insects and birds using the area. Information around the churchyard Information boards were installed to explain the changes taking place and why they matter. Reducing harmful chemicals and plastics The Eco Church page and trail describe work to phase out chemical herbicides and pesticides harmful to wildlife, and reduce new or single-use plastics. The trail says churchyard herbicide use had been phased out in favour of a weed burner for paving. Sustainable flower arranging The parish stopped using floral foam and trained flower arrangers to support stems with crumpled chicken wire instead. A living churchyard Churchyard & Wildlife These examples and counts are drawn from the supplied Churchyard Trail (2024) and the earlier Eco Church page. They are records from those sources, not a new survey. Four bat species Serotine, Common Pipistrelle, Soprano Pipistrelle and Brown Long-Eared bats are recorded in the Churchyard Trail. 251 lichen species The 2024 Churchyard Trail says 251 lichen species had been found in the churchyard. Slow worms The trail records slow worms in the churchyard and explains the rotational mowing approach that leaves areas undisturbed. Pond and pollinators The trail describes dragonflies, damselflies and pond insects at the seasonal pond, as well as birds using it. Earlier wildlife records The earlier Eco Church page listed 120 flowering plants and 15 butterfly species in its first-year records; it said records for bees, birds, mammals and reptiles were still to be collated. title: Our History
documentTitle: Our History | St Michael & All Angels
description: Explore the story of Christian worship in Mickleham, from the Domesday Book to the life of the parish today.
content: Our parish Our History Christian worship has taken place at this site for more than a thousand years. The history of St Michael and All Angels is closely connected with the history of Mickleham itself. A story across the centuries A place of worship through time The parish’s historical account describes a church whose story reaches back more than a thousand years. The details below preserve that account, including where it expresses a historical interpretation. Early history Saxon traces The parish history describes the original church as a small Saxon nave and chancel. It says traces of early work remain and suggests some may date to around 950. 1086 A church in Domesday The Domesday Book entry quoted by the parish records a church and two acres of meadow at Mickleham. c. 1180 Norman work The old parish history dates much of the present church to the Norman period, around 1180. It points to the chancel arch, lancet windows and font as important historic features. c. 1300 The Norbury Chapel The side chapel, now called the Norbury Chapel, is described as dating from around 1300. The parish history also records the Wyddowsoun tomb and brasses there. 1823–1891 Restoration and change The church underwent significant alterations: nave arches and piers were replaced in 1823, later work followed in the nineteenth century, and the north aisle was dismantled in 1891. The parish’s original history reflects on what was changed and what remains. 1913 The bells The parish account says four of the larger bells completing the peal of six were given in memory of Sir James Lawrence in 1913. Today A living parish St Michael and All Angels continues as a place of worship and community life for Mickleham and Westhumble. Explore the building Mickleham War Memorial Churchyard history Historic features and further reading The parish account also describes the chancel’s “weeping” alignment, medieval tombstones beside the north door, the Flemish pulpit, carved plaques and six bells. It records a watercolour of the church by J. M. W. Turner held by Tate. These details are drawn from the previous parish history and have not been independently reassessed during this content migration. For research into Mickleham and Westhumble, the old site points to a guide to the oldest part of the churchyard and to the Mickleham & Westhumble Local History Group.

title: Privacy & GDPR
documentTitle: Privacy & GDPR | St Michael & All Angels
description: This is the Data Privacy Notice of the Parochial Church Council (PCC) of St. Michael and All Angels Church, Mickleham.
content: ← About our parish Privacy & GDPR Privacy & GDPR This is the Data Privacy Notice of the Parochial Church Council (PCC) of St. Michael and All Angels Church, Mickleham. Data Privacy Consent Form General Data Protection Regulation Data Privacy Notice The Parochial Church Council (PCC) of St. Michael and All Angels Church, Mickleham (St. Michael’s) 1. Your personal data - what is it? Personal data relates to a living individual who can be identified from that data (for example a name, address, email address, photographs or videos). Identification can be by the information alone or in conjunction with any other information in the data controller’s possession or likely to come into such possession. The processing of personal data is governed by the General Data Protection Regulation (“the GDPR”). 2. Who are we? The PCC of St. Michael’s is the data controller (contact details below). This means it decides how your personal data is processed and for what purposes. 3. How do we process your personal data? The PCC of St. Michael’s complies with its obligations under the GDPR by keeping personal data up to date; by storing and destroying it securely; by not collecting or retaining excessive amounts of data; by protecting personal data from loss, misuse, unauthorised access and disclosure and by ensuring that appropriate technical measures are in place to protect personal data. We use your personal data for the following purposes: To enable us to meet all legal, contractual and statutory obligations (which include maintaining and publishing our Electoral Roll in accordance with the Church Representation Rules). To carry out comprehensive safeguarding procedures (including due diligence and complaints handling) in accordance with best safeguarding practice from time to time with the aim of ensuring that all children and adults-at-risk are provided with safe environments. To enable us to provide a voluntary service for the benefit of the public in a particular geographical area as specified in our constitution. To administer membership records. To fundraise and promote the interests of the charity. To manage our employees and volunteers. To maintain our own accounts and records (including the processing of Gift Aid applications). To inform you of news, events, activities and services running at St. Michael’s. To share your contact details with the Diocesan office so they can keep you informed about news in the Diocese and events, activities and services that will be occurring in the Diocese and in which you may be interested. 4. What is the legal basis for processing your personal data? Explicit consent of the data subject so that we can keep you informed about news, events, activities and services and keep you informed about diocesan events. Processing is necessary for carrying out legal and contractual obligations in relation to Gift Aid. Processing is carried out by a not-for-profit body with a religious aim provided: the processing relates only to members or former members (or those who have regular contact with it in connection with those purposes), and there is no disclosure to a third party without consent. 5. Sharing your personal data Your personal data will be treated as strictly confidential and will only be shared with other members of the church in order to carry out a service to other church members or for purposes connected with the church. We will only share your data with third parties outside the parish with your consent. 6. How long do we keep your personal data? 1 We keep data in accordance with the guidance set out in the guide “Keep or Bin: Care of Your Parish Records” which is available from the Church of England website [see footnote for link]. Specifically, we retain electoral roll data while it is still current; Gift Aid declarations and associated paperwork for up to 6 years after the calendar year to which they relate; financial records for a minimum period of 7 years to support HMRC audits; Charity Commission audits and parish registers (baptisms, marriages, funerals) permanently. 7. Your rights and your personal data Unless subject to an exemption under the GDPR, you have the following rights with respect to your personal data: The right to request a copy of your personal data which the PCC of St. Michael’s holds about you. The right to request that the PCC of St. Michael’s corrects any personal data if it is found to be inaccurate or out of date. The right to request your personal data is erased where it is no longer necessary for the PCC of St. Michael’s to retain such data. The right to withdraw your consent to the processing at any time. The right to request that the data controller provide the data subject with his/her personal data and where possible, to transmit that data directly to another data controller, (known as the right to data portability), (where applicable). The right, where there is a dispute in relation to the accuracy or processing of your personal data, to request a restriction is placed on further processing. The right to object to the processing of personal data, (where applicable). The right to lodge a complaint with the Information Commissioners Office. 8. Further processing If we wish to use your personal data for a new purpose, not covered by this Data Protection Notice, then we will provide you with a new notice explaining this new use prior to commencing the processing and setting out the relevant purposes and processing conditions. Where and whenever necessary, we will seek your prior consent to the new processing. A form for your preferences Data Privacy Consent Form Use this form to tell St. Michael and All Angels Church which contact methods and information-processing purposes you consent to, as described in the form. Download Data Privacy Consent Form (PDF) 9. Contact Details To exercise all relevant rights, queries or complaints please in the first instance contact: The data controller The Data Controller, the PCC of St. Michael’s Email admin@micklehamchurch.org.uk Telephone 01372 376443 St. Michael and All Angels Church Old London Road Mickleham Surrey RH5 6DU Information Commissioner’s Office You can contact the Information Commissioners Office on 0303 123 1113 or via email https://ico.org.uk/global/contact-us/email/ or at the Information Commissioner's Office, Wycliffe House, Water Lane, Wilmslow, Cheshire. SK9 5AF. Details about retention periods can currently be found in the Record Management Guides located on the Church of England website at: https://www.churchofengland.org/more/libraries-and-archives/records-management-guides Back to About our parish

title: Safeguarding
documentTitle: Safeguarding | St Michael & All Angels
description: The following policy was agreed at the Parochial Church Council (PCC) meeting in September 2026 and is reviewed annually.
content: ← About our parish Safeguarding Safeguarding The following policy was agreed at the Parochial Church Council (PCC) meeting in September 2026 and is reviewed annually. The Parochial Church Council (PCC) of St. Michael and All Angels Church, Mickleham (St. Michael’s) Our safeguarding commitments This policy statement actively underpins all safeguarding work within the church. In accordance with the Church of England Safeguarding Policy our church is committed to: Promoting a safer environment and culture Safely recruiting and supporting all those with any responsibility related to children, young people and vulnerable adults within the church Responding promptly to every safeguarding concern or allegation Caring pastorally for any victims/survivors of abuse and other affected persons Caring pastorally for those who are the subject of concerns or allegations of abuse and other affected persons Responding to those who may present a risk to others How the parish keeps people safe The parish will: Create a safe and caring place for all Have a named Parish Safeguarding Officer (PSO) to work with the incumbent and the PCC to implement policy and procedures Safely recruit, train and support all those with any responsibility for children, young people and adults to have the confidence and skills to recognise and respond to abuse Ensure that there is appropriate insurance cover for all activities involving children and adults undertaken in the name of the parish Display in church premises and on the Parish website the details of who to contact if there are safeguarding concerns or support needs Listen to and take seriously all those who disclose abuse Take steps to protect children and adults when a safeguarding concern of any kind arises, following House of Bishops guidance, including notifying the Diocesan Safeguarding Adviser (DSA) and statutory agencies immediately Offer support to victims/survivors of abuse regardless of the type of abuse, when or where it occurred Care for an monitor any member of the church community who may pose a risk to children and adults whilst maintaining appropriate confidentiality and the safety of all parties (after taking advice from the DSA) Ensure that Health and Safety Policy, procedures and risk assessments are in place and that these are reviewed annually Review the implementation of the Safeguarding Policy, Procedures and Practices at least annually Working together Each person who works within this church community will agree to abide by this policy and the guidelines established by this church.
